- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next period’s forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment swings from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward — force a 1–2% downward correction in the 3rd–5th period of forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently > 10% above true mean over 3–5 periods, reduce forecast by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., -0.30 to +0.30) triggers early mean reversion — reduce forecast by 2–3% in first 2 periods after sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates downward moves when sentiment is negative and price is trending up — add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.30 and price > 75.00.
